messages:
kai: Heads-up — after yesterday's packing change + AWQ switch we saw a regress in 8-bit tail latency on the small-chat workload (p95 +14%, p99 +22%). Not across all models but consistent for longer contexts (>1024).

mona: ugh, thanks for flagging. Which commit? link: https://gh/redwood/infra/commit/abcd1234

kai: the packer now does grouped packing eager during init instead of lazy streaming, commit abcd1234. I added a microprofile for the runtime:

```
Model: redwood/gpt-small-int8-awq-group32
HW: a100-40
Seq: 1536
Batching: dynamic 8ms window
KV mode: streaming
p50: 22ms
p95: 98ms (baseline 86ms)
p99: 210ms (baseline 172ms)
packing_overhead_avg: 1.9ms -> used to be 0.6ms
kernel_dispatch_time increased by ~8%
```

james: packing_overhead jump stands out. Did packer block the main inference thread?

kai: looks like packer takes a lock while building contiguous weight pages; with group-size 32 it copies more frequently. AWQ packing code ends up doing an extra memcpy for each group on first use.

nina: can you paste the profiler flame for the call path?

kai: pasted — see snippet:

```
# simplified stack samples (hotspots)
1) model_infer -> prepare_kv_cache
2) prepare_kv_cache -> pack_weights_if_needed (+15%)
3) pack_weights_if_needed -> memcpy_group -> quant_dequant_helper
4) kernel_dispatch -> select_kernel_by_dtype
```

mona: interesting that select_kernel_by_dtype also moved up. Are we falling back to a slower kernel for some sequence lengths after packing?

kai: exactly. For sequences >1024 the kernel selector chooses the fallback int8-kernel with safe-alignment checks because packed weight pages aren't 64B-aligned after the eager packing routine. The old lazy streamer preserved alignment.

james: alignment bug would explain both memcpy and kernel fallback. Any quick repro?

kai: repro script: `./bench --model gpt-small --quant awq --groupsize 32 --seq 1536 --batch 1 --kv streaming`

perf-bot: nightly/quant-bench #177 ran: gpt-small awq group32 seq1536 p95=97.8ms p99=211.3ms (regression vs baseline tag v2026-03-10)

nina: what about group sizes? AWQ group32 vs group64 tradeoffs?

kai: ran matrix: group size | packing_us | p95 | p99
 - 16 | 240us | 90ms | 183ms
 - 32 | 1900us | 98ms | 210ms
 - 64 | 1200us | 92ms | 188ms

Note: numbers are microbench for packing + latency. group32 oddly worse due to our small-block memcpy path hitting a slow branch.

mona: that's surprising — group32 is usually the sweet spot for AWQ quality/cost. Could be codepath optimized for 64 byte aligned groups.

james: kernel selection heuristic: currently we do `if (packed_mem % 64 != 0) fallback_kernel()`. Maybe too strict. We can try relaxed alignment check or copy-once aligned buffer only for the first kernel.

nina: also check KV cache policy. If packing happens during first token of many sessions, repeated per-session pack calls add up. Should we persist packed pages in a per-model attr map?

kai: we have a per-instance cache but we evict on low-memory. However many small sessions trigger pack on cold-start concurrently causing thundering herd. Batched packing would help.

mona: proposals:
- fix alignment layout in packer to guarantee 64B alignment for group sizes 16/32/64
- change packer to allocate aligned page and move memcpy out of hot path (async pack + pointer swap)
- kernel selector: tolerate misalignment for the fast kernel for x86/a100 by using unaligned load paths (safe on GPU)
- add per-model packed-pages memo and a singleflight lock to dedupe concurrent packs

james: I can prototype an async packer that enqueues a task and returns a placeholder pointer; once ready we swap. Need to keep correctness for first few tokens (stall once). Should reduce blocking by ~1.6ms in our numbers.

nina: also run calibration bench with GPTQ vs AWQ. Maybe AWQ-group32 quant layout interacts poorly with our packer. Can we test GPTQ group32/64?

kai: GPTQ group64 looked slightly faster overall because we avoid the small memcpy loop; baseline p95 ~88ms. I'll kick a matrix: AWQ/GPTQ x groupsize x kv-mode x batch-window.

perf-bot: scheduled job: quant-matrix/1771234 starting. ETA ~45m

mona: action items:
- james: prototype async pack+aligned allocation (PR) — target EOD
- kai: run the full matrix and capture per-op profiler samples (pack/memcpy/select_kernel) — today
- nina: check kernel selector policy and run fallback-free test by forcing aligned buffers — today

kai: one more note — batching heuristics interplay: dynamic 8ms window tends to coalesce many arriving short sessions; if pack happens during batch formation it inflates the whole batch latency. Maybe we should pack ahead for popular model variants (warm packing).

mona: agreed. Put warm packing behind a config flag per deployment so Dedicated customers can pre-warm. Also log a metric for pack_time so we can alert on regressions.

james: I'll open a PR with a synthetic benchmark showing async pack lowers p95 by ~12% for seq1536 on a100. will tag for review.

kai: thanks — will follow up with the full profiler dumps. :thumbsup:
